name: llmc_gpt2_train
goal: Port gpt2_train_harness.cu (llm.c's train_gpt2_fp32.cu, the fp32 GPT-2 training program, which it includes) to idiomatic SYCL 2020 with zero dpct helpers, computed on the SYCL device. Keep the program's contract: `build/candidate <debug_state.bin> <output> build/gpt2_124M.bin` loads the GPT-2 124M weights, runs 10 training steps on the debug batch (each: a forward pass with targets, zero the gradients, the backward pass, then the AdamW update with lr 1e-4, beta1 0.9, beta2 0.999, eps 1e-8, weight decay 0.01, t = step + 1), and writes raw float32: the mean loss of each step's forward pass, 10 values, exactly as the CUDA main does. A hidden reference checks the output against PyTorch's within 0.01 absolute (llm.c's own test tolerance), so use precise math (sycl::exp, not native::exp). cuBLAS calls go to oneMath (oneapi::math::blas::column_major gemm and gemm_batch, #include <oneapi/math.hpp>; the compile flags already link -lonemath). Success requires compile, verify and a zero-helper scan_helpers of the whole work directory (path '.') on the same sources: delete migrate's output under migrated/ (delete_file) once your own port is done. The files are long: read them in parts (read_file offset/limit).
reference_build: mkdir -p build && ln -sf {task_dir}/gpt2_124M.bin build/gpt2_124M.bin && g++ -O2 -std=c++17 {task_dir}/gpt2_ref.cpp -o build/reference

museport.note: B=4, T=64 debug batch from gpt2_124M_debug_state.bin; the loss of each of 10 AdamW steps checked against PyTorch's within 1e-2, as test_gpt2_fp32.cu does
